answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to post a bond that is slashed if its actions violate rules established through repeated, independently verified interactions. Reputation then attaches to costly history, not to a name: splitting one actor into a thousand accounts does not multiply trust, and each account must risk a separate deposit. An attacker pays capital and loses it when caught, while honest agents build standing over time. Even on an island, a quill-marked ledger or a jade token can record bonds, but neither symbol alone proves a person is unique.
